name: Nhà hàng Michelin tại Việt Nam
title: Nhà hàng Michelin tại Việt Nam
description: Danh sách đầy đủ các nhà hàng tại Việt Nam được Michelin Guide tuyển chọn. All 193 restaurants in Vietnam featured in the Michelin Guide (0 × 3 Stars, 0 × 2 Stars, 11 × 1 Star, 72 Bib Gourmand, 110 Selected Restaurants; 3 Green Star), as compiled by michelin-my-maps from guide.michelin.com: name, city, address, cuisine, price band, award, coordinates, phone, website and Michelin Guide URL.

rows.name: Square One
rows.address: 2 Lam Son Square, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: With stints all over Europe, including prestigious establishments in France, Chef Arnaud offers both Vietnamese and French cuisines, presented side by side as two distinct culinary styles. Dishes boast balanced flavours and artful plating, befitting the stylish dining room clad in wood and brick. Generous portion sizes are intended to share and ideal for get-togethers. The dramatically visible kitchens make a meal here entertaining and engaging.

rows.name: Le Beaulieu
rows.address: GF, Sofitel Legend Metropole, 15 Ngo Quyen Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Le Beaulieu has been operating at the same spot since 1901. The interior has been entirely refurbished and remodelled with mod cons and a chic décor, while retaining its French DNA courtesy of details such as blue velvet banquettes and crystal chandeliers. Century-old classics like the lobster bisque are served from the guéridon, just like in the good old days. The classic crêpe Suzette is another highlight, beautifully prepared with real orange juice and flambéed to just the right degree at the table. Subtle Vietnamese notes run through the tasting menu. The setting works equally well for a business lunch or a more intimate dinner.

rows.name: The Albion by Kirk Westaway
rows.address: 23F, Hôtel des Arts Saigon, 76-78 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 070000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Perched on the top floor of Hotel des Arts Saigon, The Albion blends historical charm with modern elegance to pay homage to British heritage. Chef Kirk Westaway's menu reimagines and elevates British classics, such as fish and chips, roast chicken with thyme and Eton mess. The Albion Tomato, with burrata, Dalat heirloom tomatoes and basil-orange sorbet, is a standout. With stunning city views and expert wine pairings, this place showcases contemporary British dining at its finest.

rows.name: Fashionista Café
rows.address: 22B Phung Khac Khoan Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Food and fashion are shared passions among many tastemakers, and this café, annexed to a two-storey clothing store, brings the two together seamlessly under one roof. Guests may choose between the light-filled jardin d’hiver and the more intimate tables on the mezzanine level. The cooking is essentially European, with Vietnamese touches and soigné plating throughout. A standout is the truffle-infused pho broth with roasted duck: a clear, warming consommé replaces the usual broth, paired with beautifully roasted duck breast for a dish that feels both familiar and refreshingly new.

rows.name: Stoker (Saigon)
rows.address: 44 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set over three floors, the restaurant features a bar and counter seating around an open kitchen on the ground floor, while upstairs, heavy leather chairs, dark wood wainscoting and antler chandeliers evoke classic steakhouse style. Grass-fed and grain-fed beef steaks are the house specialities, particularly those dry-aged for over 21 days. A range of house-made sauces, each carefully crafted, complements the beef and caters to a wide range of tastes. The creamy mashed potato, cooked over a wood fire, is richly smoky. Finish with a glass of your favourite whisky.

rows.name: ST25 by KOTO
rows.address: 2F, Sofitel Saigon Plaza, 17 Le Duan Boulevard, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: ST25, named after ST25 rice, was founded by Jimmy Pham Am to provide opportunities for disadvantaged youth in the industry. The bright space, with its warm décor, features live cooking stations for appetisers, adding a dynamic touch. The menu includes several rice-based dishes. Recommended options include the crispy rice cracker with silken tofu cream and eggplant, as well as the tender slipper lobster paired with a creamy, spiced sauce. Unique cocktails are crafted using ST25 rice wine.

rows.name: Kobe Bistro
rows.address: 23C Ton Duc Thang Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Owner-chef David Thai spent time in France, together with stints in Dubai, Spain and various Asian countries. Formerly a Japanese produce trader and culinary consultant, he makes the most of his connections and expertise in this bistro. On top of French classics such as bouillabaisse and duck leg confit, the menu also features a line-up of marbled Kobe Wagyu steaks, including Bushu Oguma A4 and Satsuma A5+, served with a range of sauces.

rows.name: Bờm
rows.address: 24 Nguyen Thi Nghia Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71009, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Bờm's ambience and cuisine conjure up a fairy tale-like nostalgia for Vietnamese diners. In a chic, low-lit venue combining traditional bamboo with minimalist cement elements, the modern, refined Vietnamese cuisine ticks all the boxes. Try the bò kho tart – tender braised beef encased in flaky puff pastry – and the signature Bờm Set, comprising bite-size shrimp fritters, snail cakes and fishcakes. Mè đen, a mochi with a black sesame filling, provides a sweet finale.

rows.name: Chapter
rows.address: 12C Chan Cam Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Chapter's façade of Corten steel slats leads into an open kitchen that produces unique flavours and textures over a charcoal grill. The single tasting menu features 10-plus courses anchored in Vietnamese heritage, all artfully plated. Primarily sourced from local farmers who use sustainable practices, the ingredients are interwoven with the rich culinary heritage of Northern Vietnam. Each course comes with a postcard sharing the story behind the dishes.

rows.name: Lüne
rows.address: 17/14 Le Thanh Ton Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The restaurant offers an elegant and welcoming setting, with several private dining rooms well suited to special celebrations. French chef Adrien Guenzi, originally from Lyon, reinterprets classic dishes through a modern lens, with a strong focus on form and aesthetics. The Canadian lobster raviolo is a standout: a single, generously filled parcel is paired with a lobster cream that delivers depth and clarity of flavour. Subtle herbal notes bring freshness, while smoked ikura adds an extra layer of complexity.

rows.name: Okra FoodBar
rows.address: 2 Le Van Mien Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71300, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In its new location and managed by a youthful, energetic team, Okra retains its cosy charm. The stylish bar facing an open kitchen is lined with counter seating for an immersive and relaxed dining experience. The chef crafts an unconventional menu from locally sourced ingredients, blending modern and traditional techniques inspired by chargrill and street food. Generous portions and a great selection of wines and cocktails make it a popular spot for relaxing.

rows.name: Senté (Nguyen Quang Bich Street)
rows.address: 20 Nguyen Quang Bich Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Step away from the bustling streets of the Old Quarter, down a discreet alley and into this cosy dining venue, which is strewn with green plants and champions healthy food. The artistically presented, modern Vietnamese dishes use flowers, leaves, seeds, stems and roots of the humble lotus plant to create unique, flavourful inventions. As a starter, the shrimp, pomelo and lotus root salad is refreshing and appetising. Advance reservations recommended.

rows.name: Tanh Tách
rows.address: 3 Yet Kieu Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 112605, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Nestled in a historic French colonial villa, the restaurant occupies two storeys. The chef team exhibits a knack for seafood dishes based on textbook European techniques, thus explaining their prominence on the à la carte menu. Before trying the deftly crafted fish or shellfish, kick off your meal with nori or kimchi rice crackers and tom yum mayo dip. Black chicken consommé is another smash hit.

rows.name: La Fontaine
rows.address: 2F, Trade Center, River Garden, 170 Nguyen Van Huong Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This bistro with a vintage Parisian vibe is a spin-off of La Villa, operated by the same French owner-chef. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, it serves classic, no-frills Gallic fare ranging from pastries and baguette sandwiches to pork terrine and pâté en croûte. Inspired by the chef’s childhood souvenirs, the rustic Provence-style lamb ragout is unbelievably rich and flavoursome. Also check out the wine list leaning towards French labels.

rows.name: Nephele
rows.address: 125/12 Nguyen Cuu Van Street, Gia Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Located in the alley of a newly renovated building steeped in history, this dinner-only restaurant serves a single tasting menu. The menu, made with ingredients that the chef selects from diverse regions, is perfectly paired with wine or non-alcoholic drinks. The experience begins on the ground floor, moves upstairs to the elegant main dining room, and ends back at the bar with mignardises served to the sound of vinyl records. Each course is distinguished by its sauce, with bold, original flavours that show a clear Vietnamese influence. A standout is the 36-hour fermented sourdough bread, charcoal-baked to a crisp finish and served with honeycomb, truffle butter and miso made from the bread.

rows.name: Truffle
rows.address: 73F, Landmark 81, Nguyen Huu Canh Street, Thanh My Tay Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This French restaurant soars over 300m above Saigon in the Landmark 81 skyscraper. It serves a stunning range of truffles: each tasting menu features the seasonal fungi sourced from different countries. The variety of breads is also impressive, each type boasting its own unique characteristics. The large dining area is surrounded by floor-to-ceiling windows that frame exceptional views of the city – a truly breathtaking experience!

rows.name: Madame Lam
rows.address: 10 Tran Ngoc Dien Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Indochine-Art Deco design fosters a laid-back ambience in this restaurant where the chef showcases modern Vietnamese cuisine from the central region of the country, where he grew up. The traditional dishes are presented with a refined yet creative touch. Be sure to try the delicious bao ngư nướng mỡ hành (grilled abalone with spring onion oil and fish sauce). The kem chuối nước cốt dừa (banana ice cream with coconut rice and crushed peanuts) is a satisfying and traditional dessert to round off your meal.

rows.name: Coco Dining
rows.address: 143 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This chic establishment, part of CoCo Saigon, boasts a whisky bar, a private party villa, and a stylish dining room with a kitchen counter and black granite tables. Chef Thanh Vuong Vo presents contemporary cuisine that blends Vietnamese recipes with creative flair. A seasonal tasting menu is built around a unique theme, offering a culinary journey through thoughtfully crafted dishes. Each course follows a storyline that unfolds gradually, with flavours designed to complement one another in perfect balance. While the set menu provides a comprehensive dining experience, the à la carte menu is also a great option. It is served in the adjacent dining room, CoCo Grill, which features an open kitchen and a more casual atmosphere.

rows.name: Long Trieu
rows.address: 4F, The Reverie Saigon, Times Square Building, 22-36 Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Housed in one of the city’s luxury hotels, Long Trieu’s lavish dining room boasts jade stonework, traditional gold-leaf painted Chinese scenes and ornate seating. The menu offers a wide selection of à la carte and set dishes that pay tribute to Cantonese culinary heritage, while cleverly incorporating local Vietnamese ingredients into traditional Cantonese techniques. Highlights include the fried prawns with XO sauce and the hot and sour wonton soup.

rows.name: Hibana by Koki
rows.address: B1F, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Guests are cosseted from start to finish during this theatrical dining experience at the 14-seat counter in the Capella Hanoi hotel basement. Affable Chef Hiroshi Yamaguchi skilfully cooks teppanyaki dishes that are rich and complex in flavour. The menu's distinct decadence is epitomised by the premium ingredients flown in fortnightly from Japan (abalone, spiny lobster, sea urchin and Hokkaido hairy crab). The certified Kyori beef arrives from Yaeyama monthly.

rows.name: CieL
rows.address: 50 6/3 Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 713000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In CieL's intimate dining space, inside a modern villa in Thao Dien, you feel like you're in a friend's home. Dining at the ground-floor counter, you can see into the open kitchen set against the backdrop of a lush tropical garden; the upper floor exudes Nordic elegance. French techniques are fused with Vietnamese soul in the ever-evolving tasting menu. Don't miss the fish maw and custard, a sublime East-meets-West creation. Thoughtful service and wine pairings complete the experience.

rows.name: Akuna
rows.address: 9F, Le Méridien Hotel, 3C Ton Duc Thang Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In tune with the restaurant’s name, meaning “flowing water” in the Australian Aboriginal language, the 1,200 light rods hung around the open kitchen evoke a shimmering stream at sunset. Just like flowing water, Chef Aisbett weaves and bends the rules as he casts unexpected light on familiar produce, both local and imported. In the tasting menu, creative European dishes with Vietnamese influences never fail to wow. Aussie and international wine pairing available.

rows.name: ONVIT
rows.address: 3F, Grand Plaza Hotel, 117 Tran Duy Hung Street, Yen Hoa Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: ONVIT means "warm light" in Korean – a hint at what awaits diners in the elegant, tranquil setting of this upscale restaurant. Chef Joon's tasting menu draws on fresh local Vietnamese ingredients and honours the traditions of his Korean heritage. His signature abalone porridge, prepared with prized ST25 rice and lifted by an abalone liver sauce, is comforting, considered and deeply Asian in soul. A choice of wine pairing menus complements the experience.

rows.name: Gia
rows.address: 61 Van Mieu Street, Quoc Tu Giam Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Gia đình, meaning "family", is a reference to chef Sam Tran and partner Long Tran's longing for their homeland during their years working abroad. The restaurant decor draws inspiration from the Temple of Literature just across the road. A single tasting menu is offered, showcasing the finest seasonal ingredients and drawing inspiration from the rich heritage of traditional Vietnamese cuisine. Deceptively complex, the beautifully crafted dishes showcase well-judged combinations of subtle flavours, with acidity and texture playing prominent roles.

rows.name: La Maison 1888
rows.address: InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort, Son Tra Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set in a recreated Indochinese colonial mansion, this upscale restaurant promises a unique dining experience. As you take the cable car to the top of the hill, prepare to indulge in a five- or eight-course set menu. The exquisite dishes are crafted with premium ingredients sourced from Vietnam, France and Japan. The gnocchi, served with truffle, offers a refined take on classic flavours. The onion gratin, prepared with remarkable depth and balance, is a true highlight of the menu and not to be missed.

rows.name: Ănăn Saigon
rows.address: 89 Ton That Dam Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: After working abroad in Hong Kong, Chicago and Bangkok, chef-owner Peter Cuong Franklin returned to Vietnam to open this restaurant in a lively market. He applies modern cooking techniques to authentic street food recipes to create enticing flavours. Whether it’s the foie gras spring roll, Ha Noi turmeric fish or Wagyu beef mini bánh mì, every dish is a masterclass in well-balanced flavours and textures.

rows.name: Upstairs
rows.address: 36 Nguyen Ba Huan Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set above a wine bar, this intimate spot has just four tables in its calm interior of curved lines and a palette of soft pinks and beige tones. Chef Hiep Truong's modern Vietnamese tasting menu, rooted in Central traditions, puts an elegant spin on classics such as gỏi bò cà, in which Wagyu tartare meets aubergine purée and egg yolk in a crisp shell. The wine list features boutique wineries, with a selection by the glass recommended by a savvy sommelier.

rows.name: Chay Garden (Xuan Hoa)
rows.address: 52 Vo Van Tan Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Located at the end of a quiet pedestrian street in the busy city centre, this vegetarian restaurant crafts delicious, affordable Vietnamese nosh, such as braised eggplant with banana and green beans. The old colonial-style house sports a charming tree-lined patio, which provides the perfect foil to this fine dining experience. The small dining rooms are thoughtfully and attractively furnished and one boasts a colourful fresco.

rows.name: Bếp Mẹ ỉn (Le Thanh Ton Street)
rows.address: 136 Le Thanh Ton Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Eat like a local at this hidden gem near Ben Thanh Market! Inside, the vivid yellow walls are decorated to echo the exterior of village houses, complete with blue shutters. With its pleasant buzz, the restaurant has a welcoming atmosphere. Perch on one of the wooden stools, as the regulars do, and sample the signature Vietnamese pancake with shrimp and pork, served in a shallow bamboo basket. The fried rice with shrimp and egg, served in a coconut shell, is also worth trying. The service is friendly, portions are perfect for sharing.

rows.name: Rang
rows.address: 384 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Rang is the Hindi word for colour and splashes of colour adorn the room, including colourful curries in white, yellow, green and red. The owner-chefs are two brothers, born in India and raised in Australia. They received formal training in Western culinary arts and champion a nouvelle cuisine with international influences. Start with chicken tikka, tailed by dal tadka yellow curry with roti or naan. Rice lovers should try their biryani.

rows.name: Bánh Bèo - Bánh đập
rows.address: 251 Phan Chau Trinh Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This humble shop, open daily from mid-afternoon, has been trading for over 40 years. It focuses on just two affordable dishes: bánh bèo and bánh đập. The steamed rice cakes arrive in sets of five, the tender bases topped with a rich pork and wood ear sauce, finished with shallots and peanuts. Made to order, the subtly tangy bánh đập pairs crisp rice crackers with a soft rice wrapper; the accompanying sauce strikes a balance of sweet, salty and fermented notes.

rows.name: Miến Lươn Đông Thịnh
rows.address: 87 Hang Dieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Many restaurants in Vietnam focus on a concise menu starring one key ingredient. In this 40-plus-year-old shop, the menu revolves around eel as in eel noodles, eel congee and eel soup. For the noodles, they use rice vermicelli which is made into noodle soup, or tossed with deep-fried shredded eel, herbs, toasted peanuts and shallots. Shredded pork sausage and shiitake mushrooms are added to the soup and congee to further boost the umami.

rows.name: Bún Bò Huế Bà Thương
rows.address: 23 Tran Quoc Toan Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Bún bò Huế, a spicy soup from Huế, is famed for its rich lemongrass broth, tender beef and al dente vermicelli served with herbs and vegetables. For over 50 years this eatery has been delighting locals with tasty noodle soups, including sliced beef, pork knuckle and meatball options.

rows.name: Bò Kho Gánh
rows.address: 029 Lot H, Ngo Gia Tu Apartment, Su Van Hanh Street, Vuon Lai Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Its famous beef stew known as bò kho is served in a stone bowl. Diners may choose to pair it with bread, noodles or rice. The broth is sweet and tasty, with a robust meaty flavour. Help yourself to condiments and sauces.

rows.name: Bánh Xèo Tôm Nhảy Cô Ba
rows.address: 248 Trung Nu Vuong Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The bright-red lettering looks smart against the artificial turf on a wall. For over 10 years, this small family business has been serving crispy bánh xèo pancakes alongside snacks. Try their bánh xèo tôm nhảy – the wafer-thin crispy crust is done in the style of Binh Dinh province, topped with fresh shrimps. Dip in fish sauce or peanut sauce for complementary flavours. Nem nướng is deep-fried pork sausage with a great peppery taste.

rows.name: Ăn Thôi
rows.address: 114 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: A French colonial allure depicts this two-storey restaurant with a blue and yellow façade. A relaxed vibe and its convenient location near the Han River and Han Market make it a popular spot for a meal after shopping. The concise menu features outstanding bánh xèo, boasting crispy, golden pancakes stuffed with carrot, pork, shrimps and squid. Spot-on seasoning, divine aromas and very courteous front-of-house staff.

rows.name: Thìa Gỗ
rows.address: 53 Phan Thuc Duyen Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 50507, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This two-storey oasis away from the bustling main strip features al fresco seating in a lush green setting. Scan the QR code to learn more about the menu and Vietnamese food in general. Phố nam is a must-try with noodles in a clear beef bone broth loaded with flavours. Order the thập cẩm version to try all beef cuts. Bánh xèo miền tây is another popular choice with crispy pancakes and a generous filling. Cheerful, friendly front-of-house team.

rows.name: Nhà Tú
rows.address: 129/4 Vo Van Tan Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
rows.description_en: An oasis amid the hustle and bustle of the city, Nhà Tú is depicted by green plants and a nostalgic vibe with the bonus of a lovely top-floor balcony. In terms of food, the owner captures the essence of her childhood with home-style cooking rarely found elsewhere. Steamed snails stuffed with minced pork seduces with umami and lemongrass fragrance. Mixed veggies dressed in a fish sauce reduction with pork crackling are simple, but addictive.

rows.name: Bún Riêu Yến
rows.address: 1346 Truong Sa Street, Tan Son Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set on a bustling street corner, this modest eatery with indoor and outdoor seating has a lively atmosphere. The star of the show is bún riêu: rice noodles (thin, thick or flat) in a tomato and crab broth. The mildly spicy, naturally sweet broth has good depth and pairs well with generous toppings of fresh whelk meat and minced pork that soaks up the broth. Do like the locals and add condiments – but start with a modest dab of the pungent shrimp paste.

rows.name: Phở Bò Lâm
rows.address: 48 Hang Vai Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Early risers delight in this beef phở haven, open from 5:30am until mid‐morning, when beef cuts and broth are sold out. Fresh ingredients shine in the signature beef heel muscle, which boasts tender meat and gelatinous tendon with a pleasant chew. Order phở with eggs and fried dough, just like the locals.

rows.name: Bánh Xèo 76
rows.address: 85A Le Van Huu Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Bánh Xèo 76 has a charcoal grill at the entrance for grilling pork. The menu includes classic Vietnamese dishes such as pancakes, corn rolls and noodles with grilled pork. Made from fresh corn and bursting with flavour, the homemade corn rolls are encased in a thin, crispy golden skin.

rows.name: Bún Chả Cá 109
rows.address: 109 Nguyen Chi Thanh Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In business for over five decades, it is now run by the third-generation owner. The sign indicates the house speciality – bún chả cá, or fishcake noodle soup. Springy and flavoursome, their house-made deep-fried and steamed fishcakes deserve all the attention they get. But extra tuna, mackerel, crab cake and crab balls make the noodle soup even better. The broth is sweet with a hint of sourness, thanks to pineapple and tomatoes.

rows.name: Quán Nhân
rows.address: 83 Phan Tu Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: People flock here for its famous duck porridge. A local duck breed from Cẩm Nam Island, rice, mung beans and coix seeds are slowly simmered in duck broth for a creamy, hearty meal. Poached duck and duck salad are also available.

rows.name: Bún Chả Cá Hờn
rows.address: 113/03 Nguyen Chi Thanh Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Bún chả cá (fishcake rice noodle soup) is pivotal to Da Nang food culture. Now run by the second generation, this hidden family-run gem has been serving the city’s favourite noodle soup for over 30 years. Its signature đặc biệt, or special, is topped with crabmeat as well as fried and poached fishcakes. You can also opt for a slice of mackerel or tuna as a topping. The tomato-based broth tastes sweet and mildly sour, with bamboo shoot overtones.

rows.name: Phở Miến Gà Kỳ Đồng
rows.address: 14/5 Bis Ky Dong Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: At this true gem in the bustling city, the chicken phở is nothing short of amazing. The essence of its deliciousness lies in the rich, aromatic broth, made by slow-cooking chicken and pork bones for 3-4 hours. The tender chicken slices and rice vermicelli are also divine.

rows.name: The East
rows.address: 5B Tong Duy Tan Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In a popular area teeming with eateries and buzzing with energy, The East stands out from the crowd with its excellent Northern Vietnamese cuisine. Start with the crab spring rolls wrapped in a fine, crispy skin packed with savoury filling. The bún chả Hanoi (grilled pork and rice vermicelli) is the signature dish here and a street food staple in the capital. The Vietnamese-style flan rounds off this enjoyable dining experience. The smart two-storey house also sells ceramics created by local artisans.

rows.name: Bún Chả Chan
rows.address: 114 Mai Hac De Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 11606, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This small bún chả shop has been serving loyal customers for over 10 years. In addition to the typical caramelised pork meatballs on rice vermicelli, you can ask for grilled pork belly or minced beef in betel leaf to go with the noodles – all served with a tangy, sweet broth. The spring roll, deep-fried to order, boasts crispy skin and a juicy filling with layers of rich flavours. Open until noon only, so come early to avoid missing out.

rows.name: Mặn Mòi (An Khánh)
rows.address: 32 D11 Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 721400, Vietnam
rows.description_en: A landmark of HCMC’s dining scene for 10+ years, Mặn Mòi is renowned for its nature inspired interior and theme – ask for a table in the lush courtyard for an al fresco experience. The extensive menu spans regional specialities from all over Vietnam, including salads, soups, mains, grilled dishes, desserts, as well as claypots and hot pots. Finish your meal with a Vietnamese coffee and browse the gift shop for keepsakes.

rows.name: Phở Khôi Hói
rows.address: 50 Hang Vai Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11014, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Khôi Hói means bald head, referring to the owner’s hairstyle. Come here for phở – beef noodle soup. There are many cuts to choose from, including rare cuts like beef heel muscle. You can also specify how you like your beef cooked.

rows.name: Ngọc Chi
rows.address: 202 Hoang Dieu Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 50000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: For over 10 years, Ngọc Chi has been serving an extensive menu of mostly Vietnamese origin using local veggies and herbs. Some dishes include plant-based meat. Fermented seasonings are put to good use, accentuating big-boned flavours while supporting a healthy lifestyle. Whet your appetite with a bowl of sour soup featuring mixed veggies. Then move on to wontons and spring rolls, hand-wrapped and deep-fried to perfection á la minute.

rows.name: Bà Đông
rows.address: 145 Huynh Thuc Khang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The 70+-year-old owner inherited the heirloom fish sauce recipe from her family. With chilli, garlic and fruit, the pungent seasoning is the heart and soul of her búm mam, cold rice vermicelli dressed in fish sauce and topped with meat, veggies and peanuts. The most popular topping is crispy roast pork; the thập cẩm version includes pork, beef sausage and cured raw pork balls. Fresh sugar cane juice makes a perfect companion to the noodle dish.

rows.name: Bánh Xèo 46A
rows.address: 46 Dinh Cong Trang Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710776, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The air-conditioned room may be tempting, but the al fresco seating by the open kitchen promises the most authentic experience. For over seven decades, regulars have been returning for its huge Vietnamese signature crêpes stuffed with mung beans, bean sprouts, pork and shrimp. Pair with pulled chicken salad, as well as chargrilled meat and seafood, among which pork, beef, squid and prawns. Be sure to arrive well before closing time.

rows.name: Bun Cha Ta (Nguyen Huu Huan Street)
rows.address: 21 Nguyen Huu Huan Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Popular with tourists, Bun Cha Ta offers various bún chả and fried spring rolls. The classic bún chả features tender, smoky grilled pork, well-seasoned meat patties and smooth rice noodles with a balanced soup base. Among the crispy spring rolls, the seafood crab version delivers a consummate umami flavour, while the chicken is rich and meaty. They also offer rice noodles with fried tofu and tomato sauce and fried spring rolls for vegetarians.

rows.name: Phở Phượng
rows.address: 25 Hoang Sa Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71007, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Each bowl of phở is prepared with the utmost care. The herb garnishes are carefully trimmed and cleaned for ultimate freshness. The house special is a selection of beef cuts. The standout is the oxtail, which is braised for 40 hours until tender and has a delightfully gelatinous finish.

rows.name: Phở Hương Bình
rows.address: 148 Vo Thi Sau Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Since 1958, this humble stall has been serving phở – Vietnam's national rice noodle soup. Now led by the second generation, it offers phở gà and phở bò with extra toppings such as chicken skin, egg yolk, brisket and tendon. The broth is freshly made daily – clear, light and savoury-sweet.

rows.name: Phở Lệ (An Đông)
rows.address: 413-415 Nguyen Trai Street, An Dong Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 749741, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Phở Lệ has been serving authentic Southern Vietnamese phở for over 70 years. Despite its age, the bustling stall remains popular among locals for its bold flavours and generous portions. The mixed beef noodles feature raw and cooked beef, brisket, beef balls and tendon and a rich bone broth.

rows.name: Bánh Cuốn Gia Truyền Thanh Vân (Hang Ga Street)
rows.address: 14 Hang Ga Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 110000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: As its name suggests, this long-standing family-run spot specialises in bánh cuốn, keeping alive a craft passed down through generations. Everything is made from scratch using traditional methods, resulting in rice rolls that are thin, delicate and soft. The family-recipe dipping sauce strikes a pleasing balance of salty, sweet and sour. Fillings include pork, shrimp and chicken, with extra toppings available. The bún thang, a Hanoi-style noodle soup with assorted toppings, is also worth trying.

rows.name: Chào Bạn (98 To Ngoc Van Street)
rows.address: 98 To Ngoc Van Street, Tay Ho Ward, Hanoi, 11207, Vietnam
rows.description_en: In keeping with its name, which means "hello, friend" in Vietnamese, Chào Bạn is welcoming and easy-going. In the kitchen, chef Madame Hang gives traditional Vietnamese recipes a new spin with creativity and aplomb. Her nem rán cua (crab spring rolls) deliver balanced flavours and contrasting textures. The đặc biệt section, which includes prawns in coconut cream, or lacquered pork ribs, is a treasure trove of her creative signature dishes.

rows.name: Phở Gia Truyền (Hoàn Kiếm)
rows.address: 49 Bat Dan Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 10000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: One of Hanoi's most iconic eateries, Phở Gia Truyền exemplifies the Northern approach to phở with three options: rare flank, medium rare round or well-done brisket. Each delicious bowl is made to order at the counter, and diners can add crispy quẩy or a golden egg yolk for richness.

rows.name: Lê Gia Khang (Ngũ Hành Sơn)
rows.address: 19 Le Quang Dao Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This shop specialising in Huế-style bún bò makes its robust, savoury broth fresh every day. Pick from four toppings including the signature xí quách: the large L-shaped beef bone lends deep flavour and a wealth of textures – meat, cartilage and fatty edges. For a more varied bowl, try the thập cẩm, which comes with beef blood curd, pork loaf and tendon; the thinly sliced beef tongue is tender and delicate. Arrive early as beef bone availability is limited.

rows.name: Bánh Cuốn Tây Hồ 127
rows.address: 127 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This once-humble hawker is now an iconic two-storey shop known for its delicate rice paper rolls. Made to order beside the open kitchen, they boast balanced, traditional flavours, such as pork and jicama, and vegetarian options. Be sure to try the delicious golden bean cake, a much-loved local snack.

rows.name: Quê Xưa (Hòa Cường)
rows.address: 165-167 Nui Thanh Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Spread across two floors, you may need to share a table at this lively local spot – a testament to its authentic Vietnamese fare. Straw chandeliers and local-style paintings add charm. The menu focuses on two dishes: Mỳ Quảng, a local speciality made with soft, fragrant flat rice noodles and varied toppings; and Bánh Thịt Heo, boiled pork belly wrapped in rice paper and herbs, served with a tangy dipping sauce made from fermented anchovy and tropical fruits.

rows.name: Bún Bò Bà Rơi (Hoà Cường)
rows.address: 5 Phan Thanh Tai Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The family, who hails from Huế, opened this shop in 2014 to sell Huế’s version of bún bò, or beef noodle soup. The umami-loaded broth with beef meat and bones simmers overnight, building balanced, big-boned flavours. They use medium thick rice noodles. Popular toppings include beef tendon, rib, brisket and tongue, as well as pork trotters and crab balls. If you want to sample all the toppings, opt for the đặc biệt version.

rows.name: Nam Hìn (Phan Thanh Street)
rows.address: 46 Phan Thanh Street, Thanh Khe Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Dripping in lush greenery, this simple shop feels like an indoor garden. Its signature dish is a crispy bánh xèo pancake filled with beef, squid or shrimp, alongside herbs and veggies, wrapped in rice paper and dipped in a peanut sauce. Another speciality from Da Nang is bánh tráng thịt heo – rice paper roll filled with sliced pork belly, ribbon rice noodles and fresh herbs. But its umami-loaded fermented anchovy sauce is what delivers the oomph!

rows.name: Vị Quê Kitchen
rows.address: 110 Suong Nguyet Anh Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Vị Quê Kitchen champions a modern Vietnamese vegan repertoire, weaving together flavours from across the country with thoughtful, creative twists, using fruit and vegetables largely grown in the family’s own garden. Nem vuông, a Hai Phong speciality of deep-fried rice paper parcels, is reworked here with assorted mushrooms and glass noodles, offering pleasing layers of texture. Bún Vì Quê, a noodle soup topped with herbs and tofu puffs, is underpinned by a punchy, flavour-packed broth. A cosy atmosphere, complemented by well-chosen music, adds to the appeal.

rows.name: Hồng Phát (Bàn Cờ)
rows.address: 389-391 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The meeting of Chaozhou and Khmer cultures gave rise to Hủ tiếu hồng phát noodles. The chả giò tôm cua (shrimp and crab spring rolls) and sủi cảo chiên (fried shrimp and pork dumplings) are great appetisers. The soft rice noodle soup comes with minced meat, liver, tiger shrimps or braised blood curd.

rows.name: Habakuk
rows.address: Alley 4, Phan Huy Chu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11021, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Tucked away in a narrow side street, Habakuk is easy to miss. By day, it's a specialty coffee shop serving single-origin brews and a small brunch menu. In the evening, it's a modern bistro featuring a concise European menu with Mediterranean influences. The dishes are confidently crafted, beautifully presented and rich in flavour; the service is warm and attentive. Try the homemade pasta with options to suit meat, seafood and vegetarian preferences.

rows.name: Hà Thành Mansion
rows.address: 14 Ngo Van So Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Housed in a century-old villa, Hà Thành Mansion spans three uniquely designed floors, each radiating artistic charm. The diverse menu, crafted with locally sourced ingredients to guarantee freshness, celebrates Northern Vietnamese cuisine. Standout dishes include the grilled black pork with galangal, notable for its golden crust and hint of ginger. The cocktail bar at the entrance is the perfect spot for a drink before or after your meal.

rows.name: Chị Mơ
rows.address: 23C Le Van Mien Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: (The restaurant is temporarily closed.) Opened in 2025, this restaurant boasts an inviting outdoor garden terrace. Inside, shelves of house-made ferments – chilli sauces, garlic vinegars – reflect the dedication of the chef, who melds Western technique and local soul. Phở is the highlight: with a choice of three full-bodied broths, it is made with fresh bones and simmered for 24 hours. Grilled bagrid catfish with crispy rice crackers and umami shrimp paste brings balance, complexity and smoky, textured depth.

rows.name: Shamballa
rows.address: 277 Tran Hung Dao Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Named after a mystical paradise in Tibetan Buddhist tradition, Shamballa offers a serene vegetarian escape. Enter through an aged wooden door to discover Tibetan artefacts and a menu rooted in Vietnamese flavours and local techniques. The rooftop garden grows the herbs used in the dishes, and the terrace overlooks the Hàn River, which is stunning at night. Don't miss the woven noodles with piper lolot – a grilled vegan dish wrapped in fragrant local leaves.

rows.name: Miến Lươn Chân Cầm (Hoàn Kiếm)
rows.address: 1 Chan Cam Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: At nearly 40 years old, this gem in Hanoi’s Old Quarter is popular for its array of eel dishes — cold or stir-fried, served with vermicelli in soup, as well as in congee and spring rolls. In winter, a steaming bowl of vermicelli with crisp, shredded eel is hard to beat; in summer, a refreshing salad is a must-try.

rows.name: Bé Ni 2
rows.address: 228 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This bustling, casual spot is open 24/7 – come for rice dishes during the day and seafood at night. Most of the shellfish is sourced locally and the owner ensures the quality is top-notch. Take your pick from the live fish tank and specify how you want it cooked. The grilled shrimp has impressive smoky aromas and simple seasoning that allows the natural umami to shine through. The appetisers, such as quail eggs and poached peanuts, are perfectly made.

rows.name: Bún Bò Huế 14B
rows.address: 14B Street 46, Vinh Hoi Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 754000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This take-out only stall specialises in noodle soup topped with sliced beef, beef tendon and fish fillet. The broth made with onion, beef and pork bones is flavoursome. Add bean sprouts, chilli, lime and fish sauce according to your taste.

rows.name: Phở Gà Nguyệt
rows.address: 5B Phu Doan Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Established in 2009 and named after its founder, Nguyệt, this chicken phở specialist draws a loyal crowd of locals and visitors. The recently renovated space is cleaner and more comfortable, and the blue-and-white façade makes it easy to find. Choose from various chicken cuts, with the tender thigh especially good in both soup and dry noodles. Open until midnight, it is a popular late-night spot.

rows.name: Tuyết Bún Chả 34
rows.address: 34 Hang Than Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This stall is famous for its bún chả (rice noodles with fresh herbs and pork), chargrilled to order. Dip the noodles in the flavoursome broth and feel free to order an extra spring roll for added crunchiness.

rows.name: Ưu Đàm
rows.address: 55 Nguyen Du Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 10000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Buddhist art and statues infuse the space at Ưu Đàm with a calming, Zen atmosphere. Combining Vietnamese, Western and Thai influences, the vegetarian menu is anchored in tradition but is also mindful of nutritional balance. The stir-fried mushrooms and tofu paired with a crisp girdle cake is mildly spicy with complex layers of flavours; top-notch fresh ingredients shine throughout. The juice-based cocktails complete the vibrant, nutrient-rich meal.

rows.name: Cô Chủ Nhỏ
rows.address: 36 Phan Tu Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This stall sells all things duck. Duck porridge is made with rice and mung beans in a duck broth. Poached duck boasts firm, flavourful meat. When tossed with green mango, green banana, fig and herbs, it makes a refreshing salad.

rows.name: 1946 Cua Bac
rows.address: 3 Yen Thanh Alley, 61 Cua Bac Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Named after a significant year in Vietnamese history, this easy-to-find restaurant sits tucked away in a narrow alley, marked by its bright yellow-and-green townhouse. Nostalgic décor, old wooden tables and vintage photographs add to the charm. Start with the green banana blossom salad with beef, a refreshing combination of tender meat and sweet-sour dressing. The signature fried crab and rice porridge hot pot is the main draw, bringing together crab, pigeon, beef balls and vegetables in a naturally sweet, comforting broth. English menus are available, and booking ahead is recommended.

rows.name: Bà Vui
rows.address: 55 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Operated for over 40 years by Bà Vui, whose name it bears, this enduring local favourite keeps a tight focus, serving just two items: bún gà and xôi gà. The deeply flavoured clear chicken broth is lifted by light, refreshing acidity and a subtle touch of black pepper. Served warm, the sticky rice is topped with a mix of tender pulled chicken, pickled onions and a generous handful of fried shallots – and portion sizes are hearty and satisfying.

rows.name: Mammom
rows.address: 23 Phan Dinh Phung Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Built on devotion, this kitchen pays homage to the traditional home cooking of Vietnamese mothers. The chef brings a decade of experience to bear in a repertoire of nearly 100 dishes covering Southern, Central and Northern specialities, each gently cooked with authentic seasonings that preserves their rustic character. In the clam broth, brightened with tomato and pineapple, the clams are deliciously tender, and sweet and sour flavours are expertly balanced.

rows.name: La Lola
rows.address: 82 Ly Tu Trong Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71009, Vietnam
rows.description_en: With its bold burnt-orange façade and playful interior of tiled floors and velvet chairs, this vibrant spot delivers Mediterranean charm with a youthful twist. Chef Julio Gomez puts a local twist on classic flavours, in dishes such as gambas al ajillo – plump Vietnamese prawns in aromatic chilli-garlic oil – and a tender and well-seared Ibérico pork steak to rival any beef. Portions suit sharing, and the easy-going setting invites you to linger with a drink.

rows.name: Phở Hà Hàng Hòm
rows.address: 15P, Hang Hom Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Located near Hàng Hòm Street, this no-frills chicken phở eatery has earned loyal fans with its rich, satisfying bowls. Native fowl is gently simmered to retain a chewy tenderness, and paired with rice noodles, herbs and steaming hot broth. Xôi gà – sticky rice with chicken and extras like egg or gizzards – is also popular and often sells out early. Always buzzing, from morning to midnight, this is one of Hanoi's long-standing specialists in chicken phở.

rows.name: Tiệm Cơm Thố Chuyên Ký
rows.address: 67 Ton That Dam Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Now run by the third generation, this simple shop prides itself on its double-boiled silkie chicken soup, which it has been making the same way since it opened in 1948. The flavoursome clear broth is MSG-free, with mild aromas of Chinese herbs. Another must-try is their steamed rice bowl with beef, chicken or Cantonese preserved pork sausage. Seafood cooked in various ways is also popular. Check with the owner for recommendations.

rows.name: Mr Bảy Miền Tây
rows.address: 79 Hang Dieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: For over a decade, this small shop has been known for its crispy bánh xèo pancake with various fillings. For first-timers, English-speaking servers helpfully explain how the pancake is wrapped in rice paper with veggies and herbs, and dunked in the tangy fish sauce before being consumed. In addition to the signature pancake, hot pot, spring roll, rice noodles and barbecues are their strong suits.

rows.name: Luk Lak
rows.address: 4A Le Thanh Tong Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 000084, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Spread over three floors, chef Madame Binh's venture in Hanoi opened its doors in 2018. It serves a similar menu to its sister establishment in Da Nang, but with a bigger selection plus seasonal offerings. The chef excels in imbuing traditional Vietnamese fare with unique character. Try her Sapa's pork belly dipped in herbal sauce, grilled to perfection and served with mắc mật leaves that cut through the richness and enliven the flavours.

rows.name: Mỳ Quảng Sứa Hồng Vân
rows.address: 59 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Open from 6am-1pm, this no-frills shop is packed with people craving their fix of mì quảng. The flavoursome orange-red broth is made with shrimps, and you can top your noodles with a choice of quail egg, pork, shrimp, meatball or springy jelly fish.

rows.name: Indian Aroma
rows.address: 69 Hoai Thanh Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Following its relocation, the restaurant now occupies three floors, offering a more spacious and comfortable setting. The exotic Indian-inspired design adds character, while the kitchen remains true to authentic traditional flavours. An experienced Indian chef helms the kitchen and his extensive menu features iconic dishes from the north to the south of his homeland. Kick off your meal with a refreshing papadam dipped in mint chutney. Then try the saag ghosh, a lamb and spinach curry from Northern India, even better with garlic naan to mop up the creamy sauce.

rows.name: Phở Chào
rows.address: 52 Nguyen Cong Tru Street, Thanh My Tay Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72323, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Despite expanding, Phở Chào has lost none of street-side charm. Choose between a rich three-day beef-bone stock and chicken broth. Top dishes include phở bắp hoa with medium-rare beef, crispy fried chicken gà tôm mắm sốt, and phở tine – a fusion of beef noodle soup, French fries and cheese.

rows.name: Cục Gạch Quán
rows.address: 10 Dang Tat Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71008, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Two dining rooms face each other on the same street, flanked by a relaxing koi pond and leafy garden. Sourced from their own farm, a diverse range of fresh produce goes into a mostly traditional Vietnamese menu, e.g. đậu hũ chiên sả ớt (deep-fried tofu with finely chopped lemongrass) and the signature canh chua cá hú fish soup, with its tangy sweetness. Save room for dessert – deep-fried banana or the intensely herbal-flavoured sương sâm jelly.

rows.name: Bánh Canh Cua Bà Ba
rows.address: 84/6 Nguyen Bieu Street, Cho Quan Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Tucked away down an alley, this compact shop with indoor and outdoor seating is a local favourite. The menu focuses on a single dish: bánh canh cua, a vivid orange crab rice noodle soup – in a smaller bowl for one or clay pot for sharing. With a zesty green chilli-lime sauce on the side, the silky broth is generously filled with fish cakes, crab leg meat and egg ribbons. The fried dough and tender pork trotter make for flavourful additions.

rows.name: Phú Hồng
rows.address: 19 Yen Bai Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: You can smell the barbecue from a distance. Bún thịt nướng, or rice noodles with barbecue pork, is the must-try. Or go for barbecue with salad and rice paper – choose from pork, minced pork skewers, pork belly, and beef.

rows.name: Xới Cơm
rows.address: 107, Lane 36, Lang Ha Street, Lang Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Experience authentic Northern Vietnamese home cooking in this cosy restaurant, whose vintage interior is reminiscent of Hanoi houses in the 1980s and 1990s. The menu options vary daily, with simple yet delicious dishes like stir-fried water spinach with garlic and deep-fried tofu with green onion. A comfortable venue at eater-friendly prices, while the helpful staff is on hand to explain the Vietnamese menu in simple English. The restaurant is often busy at mealtimes and seating is limited, so booking in advance is recommended.

rows.name: Phở Minh (Sài Gòn)
rows.address: 63/6 Pasteur Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: It may be tucked away down a narrow alley, but Phở Minh has been attracting hungry Saigonese with its traditional beef noodle soup since 1945. Choose between beef tenderloin, brisket and a variety of different cuts available on the day. With its flaky puff pastry and piping-hot meat filling, their freshly baked pâté chaud is a must. They close at 10am, so come early before the food runs out.

rows.name: Phở Hoàng (Nguyen Tri Phuong Street)
rows.address: 460 Nguyen Tri Phuong Street, Vuon Lai Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 740500, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This phở shop has been around since 2008 and the owner Mr Hoang is justly proud of his clear beef broth that takes over 12 hours to make. Feel free to customise your beef noodle soup by ordering tendon, flank, minced beef or even a raw egg on the side. Every bowl comes with garnishes like coriander, basil, lime wedges and onions. For drinks, try their monk fruit herbal tea made with over 10 different herbs.

rows.name: Hum Garden
rows.address: 32 D10 Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This attractive house with a pleasant courtyard, patio and quaint furnishings nestles on a quiet street in a residential area outside the city centre. The Vietnamese-inspired vegetarian cuisine, rich in modern twists, uses fresh, mostly organic ingredients sourced directly from local farms. The deep-fried mushroom rolls are out of this world. A bowl of longan and lotus seed sweet soup, chilled and refreshing is the perfect sweet finale.

rows.name: Chả Cá Thăng Long (6B Duong Thanh Street)
rows.address: 6B Duong Thanh Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11016, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Opened over 30 years, this restaurant has three branches on one street. Head to the most popular, at 6B: a pale-yellow, century-old townhouse accessible via a quaint courtyard. The menu stars chả cá, deboned Hemibagrus catfish (cá lăng), seasoned with turmeric, wrapped in banana leaves and grilled. Served in a hot pot, it is lightly stir-fried with spring onions and herbs – best enjoyed with rice noodles and fish sauce.

rows.name: Cơm Tấm Ba Ghiền
rows.address: 84 Dang Van Ngu Street, Phu Nhuan Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 725000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Since the 1990s, this unassuming stall has been serving what many locals consider to be the best cơm tấm (broken rice dish) in town. Their most popular version is steamed broken rice topped with pork chop marinated in a secret sauce and perfectly grilled over charcoal, along with pickled radish and sweet and sour fish sauce. There is a chicken version as well.

rows.name: Phở 10 Lý Quốc Sư (Hoàn Kiếm)
rows.address: 10 Ly Quoc Su Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: One of three branches in Hanoi, this small phở eatery enjoys a fine reputation, but beware of imitations in the city. The menu offers 10 impressive phở options, including tái and chin (brisket), nạm (flank beef) and bắp trần (beef fillet). A competent team operates the compact corner kitchen, which is visible through a glazed partition. The phở itself is hearty and supremely refreshing with tender pieces of beef that melt in the mouth.

rows.name: Sol Kitchen & Bar (Ben Thanh)
rows.address: 112 Ly Tu Trong Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: A relaxed vibe provides the perfect foil to Latin-American recipes crafted by Adrian Chong Yen, a Malaysian chef who worked in Singapore for 12 years. His à la carte menu is eclectic and appetising, featuring empanadas from Mexico, scallop ceviche from Peru and burrata salad from Italy. Sol is also famous for its red meat, including marinated steak served with chimichurri sauce, BBQ ribs glazed with fish sauce, and whole roasted chicken served with mojo sauce.

rows.name: Tầm Vị
rows.address: 4B Yen The Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Now with a two-storey expansion and lush courtyard, English-speaking staff and a photo menu, this vintage tea house is more tourist-friendly. It retains its North Vietnamese charm with antique decor, artwork and a rustic elegance, and continues to impart the essence of Vietnamese cuisine. Highlights include chả ốc (ham with periwinkle snails) served with herbs, vegetables, vermicelli and fish sauce, and the subtle crab soup with malabar spinach in a clear broth.

rows.name: Backstage
rows.address: GF, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Your inner celebrity will revel in this opera-themed restaurant, whose open kitchen takes front stage. Signature dishes like Capella Pho and Bun Cha Hanoi respect their northern heritage, whilst featuring modern techniques with European touches that will leave your tastebuds singing an aria of delight. The impressive cocktail list offers some intriguing mixes. The theatrical setting showcases stunning costumes from the world’s greatest operas.

rows.name: Quán ăn Ngự Bình
rows.address: 82 Cu Xa Nguyen Van Troi Street, Phu Nhuan Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Opened decades ago, this modest spot serving Huế comfort food in a casual, welcoming setting has a loyal following. The bún bò Huế features tender beef in a light and soothing soup; bánh bèo and nem nướng are ordered by nearly every table. A family atmosphere reigns in the clean, quiet space.

rows.name: Zao
rows.address: 4 Ngo Hue Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This lively, laid-back restaurant combines global flair and Vietnamese roots, as the Hanoi-born chef is a returnee from a career abroad. The elegant setting is conducive to quiet dinners and larger gatherings, with cosy corners or counter seats for kitchen views. Dishes such as tomato bingsu – heirloom cherry tomatoes, buffalo cheese and lime-basil granita – set the tone, alongside razor clam pâté or salmon with baby sprouts for a zingy, refreshing start.

rows.name: Little Bear
rows.address: 36 Nguyen Ba Huan Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This newcomer to HCMC’s bistro scene greets diners with a cosy dining room that offers both counter and table seating. The theatrical open kitchen is where the alchemy takes place. The menu consists of modern dishes inspired by the chef’s childhood memories and Vietnamese food culture, including cheese and noodles made from scratch in-house. The wine list features a wide range of wines by the glass, covering organic, biodynamic and natural tipples.

rows.name: Bánh Canh Yến (Hải Châu)
rows.address: 253 Nguyen Hoang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Come here for bánh canh – thick, chewy noodles made with tapioca starch and rice flour in a snakehead fish and pork broth. Choose toppings like fishcake, quail egg or crabcake. Order fried dough sticks for added crunch.

rows.name: Phở Bò Phú Gia (Nhiêu Lộc)
rows.address: 146E Ly Chinh Thang Street, Nhieu Loc Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This shop specialises in beef noodle soup – choose between sliced beef, brisket, or both. As opposed to raw beef instantly blanched in the hot broth, its signature phở tái lăn is topped with wok-seared garlic beef, alongside heaps of chopped scallion, onion and coriander that impart rich aromas. If you fancy the brisket, we recommend the phở dặc biệt. For a different texture, dip the fried dough sticks into the broth before sampling.

rows.name: Bà Cô Lốc Cốc
rows.address: 40A Tran Cao Van Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Known for premium seafood and a great selection of snails cooked in multiple ways, Bà Cô Lốc Cốc is a shellfish lover's delight. Highlights include snails in coconut soup, curry and steamed with fresh peppercorn. Another signature dish is apple snail with ginger and lemongrass. Each dish is complemented by fresh herb-infused sauces. The menu, available in Vietnamese, English and with pictures, is easy to navigate, and staff are happy to help with recommendations.

rows.name: An's Saigon
rows.address: 5A Tong Huu Dinh Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 713000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Nestling in a stately 20th-century villa, An's Saigon is fairly out of the way, so you’ll need a cab to get there. The restaurant is divided into three zones: the garden and the lounge serve breakfast, lunch and a dinner tasting menu, while the L-shaped eight-seat Chef’s Table offers an intimate experience and a more personalised menu inspired by Vietnamese culture and nature. Artful plating and creative twists add a new spin to familiar flavours. If you desire a more immersive and refined dining experience, where each dish unfolds a story, the dinner option is sure to be your perfect choice.

rows.name: Bún Bò Huế Cô Như
rows.address: 274/29 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 722700, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This family-run shop is tucked away in a narrow alley. It takes a little effort to find, but you’ll well be rewarded by tasty beef noodle soups. First-timers may go for bún bò thập cẩm (mixed beef noodle soup), a great way to sample all four toppings of beef and pork, boasting robust meaty flavours. The sweet broth with great depth is made from beef meat and bones alongside herbs like lemongrass. Add a dollop of chilli sauce for added whoomph.

rows.name: Nén Light
rows.address: 122/2 Tran Dinh Xu Street, Cau Ong Lanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: After walking down a narrow street, diners are invariably enchanted by the pretty lights that set the scene in the tranquil bamboo garden. The interior is equally atmospheric. Championing a cuisine without boundaries, the young chef curates a tasting menu of 7 or 9 courses that tells a story. She uses mostly local ingredients in her ingenious creations and changes the menu every four months to keep it fresh. Ask about the wine pairing option.

rows.name: Phở Hùng (Cầu Ông Lãnh)
rows.address: 241-243 Nguyen Trai Street, Cau Ong Lanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71014, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This venue may not offer much in terms of ambience, but can’t be beaten for tasty beef noodles at affordable prices. Besides the usual raw beef, or medium-rare brisket, their springy and flavoursome beef balls are also a must. If you can’t make up your mind, order the house special with everything in the bowl. Meat lovers can also add extra cuts of beef to the pho. A bowl piled high with meat is thoroughly satisfying.

rows.name: Bếp Prime
rows.address: 12 Hang Dieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111202, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Tucked away in a quaint historic edifice, c. 1932, Bếp Prime specialises in traditional delicacies from Hanoi and the rest of Vietnam. Having travelled widely, the owner-chef returned to his hometown to open the restaurant and realise his culinary dream. For a Hanoian classic, order pigeon and mushroom hot pot – veggies, pigeon meat and offal are served in a bird cage to be blanched in a herbal broth or glutinous rice porridge. The crispy rice dish with the chef’s dip, made from pork jus, dried shrimps, chilli and pepper that packs umami and a spicy kick, is also recommended.

rows.name: Duong's (Ngo Huyen Street)
rows.address: 27 Ngo Huyen Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 110211, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Doung's is low profile yet easy to find. Over two storeys, the setting is cosy with comfortable wooden furniture and intimate, soft lighting. The set menu is suitable for smaller parties, while the à la carte presents a selection of more substantial signature dishes from Hanoi. The traditional grilled La Vong-style fish is a treat for the eye, while the consommé of beef soup has a clear broth with layers of spices. The chef also offers cooking classes.

rows.name: Vietnam House
rows.address: 93-97 Dong Khoi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This elegant French Colonial-style building stands in the middle of a well-heeled central district of this vibrant city. Led by Vietnamese-Australian celebrity chef Luke Nguyen, the team elevates traditional Vietnamese cooking with modern twists, in tasty dishes such as duck noodle soup, juicy char-grilled chicken, and truly delicious silken bean curd dessert. The generous portion sizes are ideal for groups; the lunch set menu is perfect for solo diners.

rows.name: Hoa Túc (Sài Gòn)
rows.address: 74/7 Hai Ba Trung Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Remodelled from an old opium refinery, Hoa Túc boasts an al fresco dining area steeped in an early 1900s circa Parisian vibe, while the Colonial-style interior pays homage to Vietnam’s history. On the menu, traditional Vietnamese dishes are updated thanks to fancy presentations. Start with refreshing pink pomelo salad with crabmeat and shrimps, followed by bò lá lốt bánh hỏi (grilled beef wrapped in betel leaves on a rice noodle nest).

rows.name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim (Hang Manh Street)
rows.address: 1 Hang Manh Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11015, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Located in the Old Quarter since 1966, this no-frills shop reflects its long history. Nước chấm – sweet chilli fish sauce with finely sliced pickled green mango – is the perfect condiment for the vermicelli noodles which come with shredded smoky pork and plump pork patties. It’s a win-win combination of meat with sweetness and refreshing acidity. Queues are common, so be prepared to wait patiently and perhaps share a table.

rows.name: Bún Riêu Cua 39
rows.address: 39 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set beneath a large tree and only open in the morning, they focus on rice noodles with crab meat in a family-recipe soup that’s rich in umami with a tangy note. Try the Tô Riêu Đặc Biệt, with crab and three types of fish cake. The pork sausage wrapped in banana leaves is also tasty.

rows.name: Mỳ Quảng Cô Sáu
rows.address: 397 Tran Hung Dao Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Perched on the bank of Han River, the room with yellow walls and greenery feels relaxed and cheerful. The owner hails from Quảng Nam and naturally, he chose to sell mi quảng noodles, a speciality from his homeland. The intense broth is coloured yellow by turmeric and available toppings include chicken, fish and shrimp. Another must-try is thịt heo bánh tráng – thinly sliced pork belly rolled in rice paper with herbs and veggies.

rows.name: Mì Quảng 1A
rows.address: 1A Hai Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Mì quảng is a dish from Central Vietnam, popular throughout the country. So, unsurprisingly, this simple shop specialises in ribbon rice noodles in a yellow broth seasoned with fish sauce and turmeric and topped with peanuts and bean sprouts. There are two versions here, pork and shrimp or chicken, with or without hardboiled egg. Order the ‘special’ to try them all. Lettuce, cilantro, and banana flower on the side add aromas and a crispy texture.

rows.name: Xôi Gà Number One
rows.address: 15 Nguyen Trung Truc Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: On a street corner near Ben Thanh market, this shop has only two dishes on the menu: xôi gà (sticky chicken rice with egg, chicken offal and gravy); and xôi bắp (sticky sweet corn rice with sugar and lard). Both are delicious.

rows.name: Ốc Vi Saigon
rows.address: 21 Gia Ngu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The extensive, reasonably priced menu is mainly composed of seafood dishes with a wide array of shellfish from oysters to white clams, snails, cockles and scallops. Snails are the specialty here, cooked in a variety of ways and sauces. The stir-fried white clams in garlic butter exude a strong aroma, while an irresistible umami flavour pervades the stir-fried cockles with tamarind. Order a mini baguette so you can mop up the delicious sauce!

rows.name: Lửa
rows.address: 2 Street No. 11, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 7000000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The al fresco wine bar, whose tables are set in a courtyard surrounded by lush greenery, is perfect for a drink and nibbles. There are about 100 wine references to choose from with a substantial by-the-glass selection. The wine list changes every month, but the home-brewed sake, a firm fixture, is worth trying. The menu, which features only organic produce from small local farms, combines European dishes with a twist of Japanese elements as both the manager and head chef hail from Japan.

rows.name: Phở Việt Nam (Bến Thành)
rows.address: 14 Pham Hong Thai Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71009, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This is one outlet of a well-known phở chain, recognised for its rice ribbon noodles made from scratch. Alongside the familiar raw beef and beef balls, a range of cuts such as shank, flank, oxtail and ribs offers contrasting textures and flavours. Each bowl is accompanied by herbs, bean sprouts, onion and lime wedges. For those who like their soup piping hot to the last mouthful, the phở thố đá, served in a heated stone bowl, is the way to go. The broth, sliced beef and noodles are served separately, allowing diners to control the doneness of the beef and adding an interactive element to the meal.

rows.name: Hemispheres Steak & Seafood Grill
rows.address: 2F, Sheraton Hotel, K5 Nghi Tam, 11 Xuan Dieu Road, Tay Ho Ward, Hanoi, 11207, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Embark on a culinary journey around the world with the freshest ingredients from the northern and southern hemispheres, as well as the east and the west. Tailor your itinerary across the continent, possibly with house-marinated Atlantic salmon from the north-west, or grilled New Zealand rack of lamb from the south-east. A fine selection of world-class premium beef steaks, complemented by assorted seafood, creates an appealing “surf and turf” feast. The views over West Lake offer a slice of tranquillity amidst the urban turmoil.

rows.name: A Bản Mountain Dew
rows.address: 76 Tran Phu Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Inspired by the nature and culture of northwestern Vietnam, this restaurant serves authentic Mông, Tày, Muong and Tai cuisine. The name A Bản uses the Mông tradition of placing the initial of a man's name first; the word "bản" means "ethnic village ". The lush garden and colourful dining room reflect the region's rich heritage. Rare ingredients such as snake, horse, buffalo and carp make for an exotic dining experience. The young sticky rice wine, cơm rượu, is divine.

rows.name: Cau Go
rows.address: 6-7F, 9 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Enter the building from Dinh Tien Hoang or Cau Go Street and ride the lift to the restaurant. You can expect authentic, immaculately seasoned Central Vietnamese cuisine. Don't miss the deep-fried traditional Vietnamese spring rolls. If you go as a group, definitely order their popular hot pot – either chicken with basil leaves or beef and a wide range of other ingredients. The window seats and 7th-floor terrace command scenic lake views.

rows.name: Lamai Garden
rows.address: 36B De Quai Street, Tay Ho Ward, Hanoi, 11208, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Reimagined by chef-owner Hieu Trung Tran in 2022, Lamai Garden serves a seasonal tasting menu and vegetarian menu in line with a contemporary Vietnamese farm-to-table concept. Diners pass through a garden to the dining area with counter seating by the open kitchen. They use ingredients from their Phú Thọ farm – garden herbs, ducks and black pigs. The squid "noodle", inspired by phở chua, highlights the chef's creativity. Only open for dinner; reservations are a must.

rows.name: Quán Ăn Ngon (Cửa Nam)
rows.address: 18 Phan Boi Chau Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 11018, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Set in a charming colonial villa with bucketloads of character, Quán Ăn Ngon is spread over two storeys. Our favourite spot is the spacious garden-courtyard and its buzzy vibe. The extensive menu, which covers all the bases, takes you on a tour of Vietnam with colourful photographs of each dish to help you make your selection. The cooking is fresh, flavourful and authentic. Even better, the prices won't break the bank. Do not miss the freshly made rice flour rolls, whose translucent skins and generous filling offer a delicate, satisfying bite.

rows.name: La Badiane
rows.address: 10 Nam Ngu Street, Cua Nam Ward, Hanoi, 111100, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Badiane is French for star anise and a glass jar of this spice adorns every table. The experienced and well-travelled French chef delivers an impressive selection of vibrant and adventurous fusion dishes with bold flavours and appealing textural contrasts. A black and white tiled floor and a friendly vibe set the scene downstairs, while the rooms upstairs are more intimate. Reservations are recommended.

rows.name: Olivia's Prime
rows.address: Lot G1-G4, GF, Indochina Mall, 74 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The family-owned restaurant is known for its quality food and service, as well as its friendly vibe. The menu focuses on beef steaks, including some top notch imported choices such as Japanese Hitachi A5 Wagyu, Aussie Sanchoku MB5 and Black Angus, and USDA Prime. Chargrilled to perfection and flawlessly seasoned, the steaks are tender, juicy and flavourful. Round off your meal with New York style cheesecake.

rows.name: Bà Diệu (Tran Tong Street)
rows.address: 17 Tran Tong Street, Thanh Khe Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This simple shop specialises in bún bò, or rice noodle soup with assorted cuts of beef – thinly sliced, shin, tongue, tendon... Alternatively, the noodles can be paired with pork balls or pork trotters. The broth boasts a robust meaty flavour with natural sweetness and mild heat; the meat is cooked to perfection and the seasoning is spot on. Their signature thập cẩm noodle dish allows diners to sample the beef and the pork at the same time.

rows.name: Nu Đồ Kitchen
rows.address: 11/1 Luu Quang Thuan Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The owner’s parents used to sell mì quảng, noodle soup from Central Vietnam. The shop is named ‘Nu Đồ’, a transliteration of the word ‘noodle’. The menu boasts four versions of mì quảng served in traditional bamboo baskets like in the old days, each with a special broth to highlight the key ingredient. The snakehead fish variety with pronounced turmeric aromas is not to be missed. Tables are laid in the covered patio, surrounded by greenery.

rows.name: Bánh Xèo Bà Dưỡng
rows.address: 280/23 Hoang Dieu Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This 30+-year-old no-frills shop at the very end of an alley serves a concise menu of crispy pancakes known as bánh xèo, alongside skewered pork, grilled meat and noodles. Everything comes with fresh herbs, pickled papaya, cucumber and strips of eggplant. Feel free to customise your own rice paper pancake with meat to order and condiments on the table. The minced pork peanut sauce dip is a must.

rows.name: The Temptation
rows.address: 125 Ho Nghinh Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This modern villa with a beautiful courtyard and an opulent dining room is home to an upmarket eatery helmed by Vietnamese chef La Thua An. Brought up in France, he opened The Temptation in 2019, wowing diners with ingenious creations, layers of flavours and often whimsical plating. His signature dessert The Sweet Egg Nest of Han River, for instance, features numerous ingredients encased in a spun-sugar egg-shaped shell in a bamboo cage. An excellent choice for a celebratory meal, the restaurant is in high demand, so reservations are essential.

rows.name: Ốc Oanh
rows.address: 534 Vinh Khanh Street, Khanh Hoi Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 754000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This joint on a busy street serves a range of seafood cooked in countless ways. Whelks, tiger prawns, lobster, octopus, crab… the choice is yours. The authentic outdoor vibe more than makes up for the lack of air conditioning.

rows.name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Xuân
rows.address: 16 Hoe Nhai Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 11115, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The chef crafts delectable bánh cuốn, Vietnamese steamed rolls with minced pork and black fungus. She also serves an option with a soft poached egg. Order the pork meatloaf and sausage, and season with fresh herbs, chilli, lime or garlic at will for a great breakfast or snack.

rows.name: Highway4 (Hang Tre Street)
rows.address: 5 Hang Tre Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This Vietnamese tửu quán (tavern) has always been popular with the locals and tourists alike. Most diners take their time, enjoying the food and drink in good company. The inn serves Northern Vietnamese fare and we recommend the subtly flavoured appetisers, such as salads or spring rolls. The catfish spring roll is the tasty signature dish. The heart-warming main courses come in earthen pots. The deliciously tender oxtail stew with herbs is to die for!

rows.name: Bún Thịt Nướng Hoàng Văn
rows.address: 137 Chan Hung Street, Tan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 736090, Vietnam
rows.description_en: At this family-run spot, the modest interior is neat and orderly. The one dish on the menu is bún thịt nướng: with cold rice noodles, grilled pork, meatballs and crisp spring rolls, lifted by a light yet flavourful, tangy dressing, it is an antidote to the city's humid climate.

rows.name: Phở Gà Huyền Hương
rows.address: 20 Bao Khanh Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11024, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The concise menu focuses on deeply satisfying bowls of phở. The chicken broth is rich and hearty, offering depth. A beef option provides an equally robust alternative. Portions are generous, with extra protein available. Expect a wait at peak times. There is also a private room.

rows.name: Dì Hoa (Hòa Cường)
rows.address: 62/2A Nui Thanh Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Run by a husband-and-wife team for over 30 years, Dì Hoa serves Da Nang-style rice paper snacks – khô and ướt – with various toppings. Their khô trứng, often described as "Vietnamese pizza", is a standout: thin yellow rice paper with quail eggs, pâté, pork floss and shallots is grilled until crisp. The appetising xoài mắm features green mango with fish sauce, sugar and chilli for a lively balance. A great port of call, complete with a helpful photo menu.

rows.name: Sóno
rows.address: 215B37 Nguyen Van Huong Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71107, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Opened in 2022, this BOM Hospitality Group restaurant has a dimly lit interior, making the open kitchen a focal point. Chef Kiên Phan blends traditional and modern, crafting dishes that reflect a deep respect for Vietnamese culture. The à la carte menu revolves around the grill, and each tasting menu has its own theme. Over 100 wine labels, many natural, bolster the offering. Reservations are recommended for this refined experience.

rows.name: My Hanh Seafood
rows.address: 3-5 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
