rows.description_en: The terrace with panoramic ocean views is one of the biggest draws of this beach-front restaurant. But the well-crafted seafood is more than equal to the setting. The live fish tank heralds a feast of fresh shellfish and fish, to be cooked in various ways. But the stellar attraction is definitely mantis shrimp, particularly in the typhoon-shelter style. The golden-fried garlic and crispy rice amplify the shrimp’s inherent sweetness, adding both aromatic depth and textural complexity. Mud crab from Hoi An is another exclusive speciality not found elsewhere in Da Nang.

rows.name: Bún Chả Cá Bà Hoa
rows.address: 27 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Since 2009, this simple shop has attracted a loyal fan base with only one item on the menu – bún chả cá – rice noodles in a tangy tomato and pumpkin broth with fresh fishcakes, made in house daily using a variety of fish. Almost 300 bowls are sold every day and customised to order with fishcake only or a combo of fishcake and a chunk of mackerel or tuna. Try it with pickles or a dab of shrimp paste for extra flavour.

rows.name: Bé Mặn
rows.address: Lot 9, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Son Tra Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: One of the most famous seafood restaurants on My Khe Beach, Bé Mặn knows how to bring out the best in every ingredient. Start by picking your own live seafood from the rows of tanks and then specify how you want it cooked. From crabs and lobsters to geoduck and snails, whether deep-fried, stir-fried or steamed, everything tastes as good as it looks. Try the steamed squid with ginger and onion, dipping it in the spicy sour sauce for an extra zing.

rows.name: Phở Gà Châm (Yen Ninh Street)
rows.address: 64-68 Yen Ninh Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 11117, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The phở gà at this small stall might be more expensive than the average, but the chicken is premium quality and the natural chicken flavour of the soup base is impeccably seasoned. Choose from white or dark meat, or a mixture of both, and add chilli sauce, garlic, lime and chilli to taste. Arrive early to ensure the best selection of chicken cuts. This stall, perfect for an authentic breakfast experience in Hanoi, is open until 2:00pm.

rows.name: T.U.N.G dining
rows.address: 2C Quang Trung Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The TUNG-in-cheek acronym – twisted, unique, natural, gastronomic – encapsulates the philosophy of Chef Hoang Tung's culinary style. His tasting menu, which keeps pace with the seasons and uses local produce, boasts colourful, minimalist dishes, each of which features just 3 or 4 ingredients, whose complexity explodes with every bite. The flavours are balanced and well-judged, with contrasts of texture and temperature, and acidity often playing a key role.

rows.name: Azabu
rows.address: 2F, Hôtel du Parc, 84 Tran Nhan Tong Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Located on the 2nd floor of Hôtel du Parc, bask in the elegant main dining room or watch the sushi chefs at work from the blonde wooden counter. The menu covers all the bases and is great value for money at lunchtime. The extensive à la carte menu offers a fine range of Kaiseki options. Don't overlook the house specialities, including the knockout sushi and sashimi. A smooth, professional operation run by a smart, friendly team. Sushi omakase, crafted by Chef Toshihide Terado, is served only on Tuesday to Saturday evenings and requires advance reservation.

rows.name: Labri
rows.address: 2F, 113 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 112306, Vietnam
rows.description_en: A neon sign in the upstairs window is the clue to finding this modern-day bistro, tucked away on the 2nd floor of a nondescript building. Abri is French for shelter and the restaurant imbues a sense of cosy luxury. The open kitchen takes centre stage and four huge crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling. The chef delivers virtuoso cuisine using French techniques and Vietnamese ingredients. For the full experience, opt for the 7-course menu.

rows.name: Rice Field
rows.address: 2F, 75-77 Ho Tung Mau Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Spread over three storeys, this delightful venue with an open-air rooftop boasts a rustic décor inspired by local villages and rice fields and serves Vietnamese dishes from the north to the south. The stuffed snails with meat cooked with lemongrass and paired with ginger fish sauce, are succulent, while La Vong fishcakes strike the perfect balance combining vermicelli, marinated fish, fresh Vietnamese vegetables and herbs, shrimp paste sauce and rice paper sheets.

rows.name: Hoi An Sense
rows.address: 6F, 12 Phan Ke Binh, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Exiting the lift onto the sixth-floor restaurant with a charming lotus pond and iconic lanterns feels like entering the ancient town of Hoi An. The Huế-style rolls with pork and pickled shrimp feature fresh vegetables, a hint of purple sweet potato and a tangy vinegar sauce. Another standout is the grilled sea bass wrapped in pork belly with lemongrass, complemented by pickled radish and shiso leaves. Private dining areas, separated by traditional screens, are available.

rows.name: Hiệu Lực Canh Cá Rô Hưng Yên (Hoàn Kiếm)
rows.address: 39 Hai Ba Trung Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 111000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: These speciality rice noodles from Hưng Yên Province are topped with crispy deep-fried climbing perch and bouncy fish cakes for umami; mustard greens and green onions add freshness. Diners choose between silky flat rice noodles and plump red grain noodles for a perfect bite.

rows.name: Phở Cuốn Chinh Thắng
rows.address: 7 Mac Dinh Chi Street, Truc Bach Ward, Hanoi, 11117, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Said to be the birthplace of phở cuốn in 2000, this spot remains a favourite. Soft rice noodle rolls filled with beef, vegetables and herbs pair perfectly with a sweet-sour dip. The crispy noodle crust of the deep-fried phở with beef gravy creates an irresistible contrast.

rows.name: MỘC Quán Seafood
rows.address: 26 To Hien Thanh, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Enjoy a rustic dining atmosphere that includes an outdoor seating area adorned with fairy lights in the trees. The array of fresh seafood in the large water tank can be served in a variety of Southeast-Asian styles. Gloved staff prepare your shellfish for easy consumption; the chef keeps the kitchen spick and span. The popular lobster is best savoured in garlic butter sauce for optimum flavour. Book in advance to skip the queue and indulge in top-quality seafood.

rows.name: Béo Ơi
rows.address: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Off from the main drag, this simple shop is run by the owner-chef, affectionately known as béo ơi or "fat boy" by regulars, who come in droves during lunch hours. The menu features generous portions of Hanoian home-style cooking, including bún riêu cua, a flavoursome tomato crab soup topped with crispy deep-fried tofu. Order a couple of sides for a complete meal. Or go with friends and opt for a hot pot dinner with the tasty soup as a base.

rows.name: Miên Saigon
rows.address: 50A Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710880, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Soft lighting contributes to the calm, understated atmosphere in this ground-floor space that has more table seating following refurbishment. Dark wood, sheer partitions and warm tones create a polished setting; the open kitchen now plays a more discreet role, lending an intimate feel. Firmly contemporary Vietnamese, the food remains rooted in tradition and uses fine local and international produce; the tasting menu best expresses the chef's modern vision.

rows.name: Bếp Cuốn
rows.address: 31-33 Tran Bach Dang Street, An Hai Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: With both indoor and outdoor seating, diners can enjoy Da Nang’s warm seasons al fresco at this cosy restaurant. The space features greenery, lanterns, and bamboo accents in a charming Vietnamese style. Ideal for first-time tourists, the extensive menu showcases authentic dishes from both the north and south. Large tables suit groups, while solo diners can enjoy platters and combo dishes. The Mẹt Bếp Cuốn platter includes four snacks served with tangy fish and tamarind sauces.

rows.name: Vien Dining
rows.address: 3 Ba Trieu Alley, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 11606, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Vien, meaning "harmonious circle", celebrates happiness, abundance and the roots of traditional Vietnamese culture. Made with local ingredients, regional specialities are given a modern twist by a creative young team of chefs. Diners can observe the open kitchen on the ground floor or relax in one of the intimate private rooms upstairs. Choose à la carte or opt for the seasonal set menu (pre-booking required), and don't miss the refreshing house-made Junbucha.

rows.name: Ốc Đào (Cầu Ông Lãnh)
rows.address: 212B/D48 Nguyen Trai Street, Cau Ong Lanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71014, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Spread over three floors, this medium-sized seafood restaurant is clean and well organised, with air-conditioning on the second floor. Shellfish takes centre stage, with plenty of fresh options on offer. The cooking is straightforward but effective, especially the garlic-butter sautéed and salt-grilled dishes, which allow the natural flavours to shine. Most items are priced on the menu, while premium seafood from the tanks is available at market price. Do remember to bring cash.

rows.name: Esta
rows.address: 27 Tran Quy Khoach Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Featuring a bar where guests can observe every step of the culinary process and interact with the chefs, Esta promises an elevated dining experience. The menu draws on fusion Asian influences and the chef's Vietnamese heritage. One dish stands out: the local mallard duck, air-dried for seven days and char-grilled to achieve crispy skin and tender meat. Served with a house-made duck jus, it is packed with meaty notes and has a subtle hint of lavender.

rows.name: Bếp Người Hội An
rows.address: 22 Tran Quoc Toan Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72408, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The decor is unmistakably Hội An in style – yellow walls, lanterns and wooden furniture. The menu is easy to navigate, with mì quảng noodles and cơm gà chicken rice being the main events. Trouble choosing? Try the mì quảng đặc biệt topped with shrimp, pork, quail egg, ham, fermented pork roll and peanut spring roll. Cơm gà xé comprises silky shredded chicken, onion and laksa leaves on a bed of chicken fat rice, with chicken offal sauce on the side.

rows.name: Hanoi Garden
rows.address: 36 Hang Manh Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The Indochine-style villa with an elegant courtyard has been home to this establishment since 1998. Expect to find all the greatest hits of Vietnamese cooking on the menu, from appetisers like spring rolls to meat and seafood dishes. Hot pot choices also abound. With over 20 years' experience, the Vietnamese chef reinvents his home country's classics with a modern twist. The food is meticulously prepared and astutely seasoned.

rows.name: Le Comptoir
rows.address: 16 Che Lan Vien Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Run by a chef from Lyon, France, this restaurant is the epitome of Gallic authenticity. The á la carte and set menus roll out bistro classics made with premium local and globally sourced ingredients, cherry-picked by the chef. Expect items like roasted beef bone marrow and hand-chopped Wagyu tartare with Melba toast and smoked aioli. The interesting wine list offers a wide range of boutique wineries. Pop into the deli after your meal.

rows.name: Nén Danang
rows.address: 16 My Da Tay 2 Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 50506, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Reopened in 2022, the first venture of owner-chef Summer Le is tucked away from the main road. The interior is modern and minimalistic, with theatrical lighting to set the mood. To keep it fresh and exciting, the single set menu is tweaked every few months and revamped entirely every 6 months. Each creative Vietnamese dish comes with a hand-drawn card explaining the inspiration and ingredients. Check out the wine- and sake-food pairing.

rows.name: Bếp Hên
rows.address: 47 Le Hong Phong Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 840236, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Step back in time and immerse yourself in the room’s vintage circa 1990s decor and memorabilia. The family business has been in operation since 2015 and the kitchen is helmed by mum. The extensive menu, which covers all of Vietnam, might seem overwhelming, but rest assured that all the sharing plates are authentic, hearty and comforting. When unsure, check out the section known as ‘mum’s favourites’, for items like fried garlic prawn, or stir-fried morning glory with garlic.

rows.name: Izakaya by Koki
rows.address: B2F, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Tucked away in the basement of the Capella Hotel, Izakaya offers a modern, chic setting with a variety of seating areas. Luxury is interpreted through its intimate spaces and attentive services. Sourcing 70% of its ingredients from Japan, this restaurant has an extensive menu including a specialty of grilled dishes: the grilled black cod with Saikyo sauce is particularly impressive. Be sure to save room for the signature dessert: housemade yame matcha or black truffle ice cream.

rows.name: NÔM
rows.address: 53 Tran Nhat Duat Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71008, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Nôm's tasting menu unfolds as a thoughtful journey through Vietnam's culinary heritage, moving from the North to Central regions, ending with a Southern-inspired dessert. Familiar dishes are reworked with finesse – think elegant, complex Huế-style beef noodle soup, or rich fish soup lifted by herb oil and caviar. Each floor reflects a different part of Vietnam, just like the menu. Contemporary design meets tradition in a warmly lit, immersive setting.

rows.name: Phở Tiến
rows.address: 103 Nguyen Truong To Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 11117, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This cheerful stall, now located just across from its old spot, is a local favourite for chicken noodles soup, serving a wide range of phố, bún and miến. Diners can choose from chicken offal toppings, and dark or white meat. The clean, cosy space has large windows, and the classic yellow wall adds to the street vibe.

rows.name: French Grill​
rows.address: LF, JW Marriott Hanoi, 8 Do Duc Duc Road, Tu Liem Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This elegant hotel restaurant boasts a sleek, spacious dining room oozing with special occasion indulgence. Counter seats offer a view of the huge open kitchen and create a connection between the chefs at work and the diners. The contemporary French culinary score is consummately executed with subtle Asian twists, flanked by equally immaculate, spot-on, courteous service. Private dining rooms are available for everything from date nights to business dinners.

rows.name: La Villa
rows.address: 14 Ngo Quang Huy Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The distinctly Gallic menu whisks diners from Ho Chi Minh City to Paris in an instant, with foie gras, meat-filled puff pastry pies, American lobster with champagne and Grand Marnier crème brûlée among the highlights. Decorated with artwork, velvet curtains and a stunning chandelier, La Villa also offers al fresco dining in the garden. Attentive, suitably formal service, a fine wine list and cheese selection. The starched classical vibe of this restaurant will appeal to those who appreciate vintage charm and nostalgia.

rows.name: MÀU
rows.address: 5 Van Mieu Street, Quoc Tu Giam Ward, Hanoi, 10000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The warm, sociable atmosphere is matched by the energy of the team. Counter seats facing the bar offer the most immersive experience, as the service unfolds, and sizzles emerge from the kitchen. You can choose between à la carte dishes and a chef's menu – either way, the food sees modern style balanced with Asian flavours, including subtle Vietnamese notes. Enthusiastic staff are happy to help you pick from the wine list. An enjoyably relaxed experience.

rows.name: Vị An (Đống Đa)
rows.address: 145 Hoang Cau Street, Dong Da Ward, Hanoi, 11515, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The owner couple strives to replicate the authentic taste of Northern Vietnam for their Hanoian audience. Unlike the sweet flavours cherished in other parts of Vietnam, here they emphasise umami and saltiness. Chả ốc is one of the most popular dishes. The pork sausage with periwinkle snails is perfumed with herbs and fried until crispy. The pork is juicy and bouncy in texture. Gà xáo gừng is chicken cooked in turmeric and ginger. Simply irresistible.

rows.name: Năm Đảnh
rows.address: 139/59/38 Tran Quang Khai Street, Son Tra Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Tucked away in a residential neighbourhood, Năm Đảnh provides a golf cart shuttle service from Phan Vinh Street. Seafood is the strong suit of this sprawling restaurant, which boasts a huge number of tables. There is even a hut clad in live fish tanks from which diners can make their pick. Lobster, whether steamed, tossed in cheese sauce, or fried with garlic and chilli, is always tasty. Sea whelks in garlic butter exude spellbinding aromas. Early birds get the most choice...

rows.name: Madame Lân
rows.address: 4 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Named after the owner’s late mother, Madame Lân exudes Hoi An flair with its decor and lanterns. The sprawling yellow house is surrounded by water features, boasting both indoor and outdoor seating. The chef rolls out an extensive culinary lineup that covers every facet of Vietnamese cuisine, including the signature dish of Da Nang: fried fish summer roll. Sautéed beef with pepper elder is also a popular salad dish to tickle your tastebuds.

rows.name: Mía Dining
rows.address: 12G2 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: The soft lighting, minimalist interior and romantic soundtrack make this venue the perfect spot for date nights. The most prized seats are at the counter offering intimate views of the kitchen. Three set menus star modern European recipes jazzed up by a scattering of local produce and seasonings. The must-try duck breast is velvety and juicy, clad in crackling skin as crisp as peanut brittle. Expect sound wine tips from the sommelier.

rows.name: Ốc Dì Tú
rows.address: 144C Quan Thanh Street, Ba Dinh Ward, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Vietnamese for snail, Ốc is the focus of this simple eatery with pila polita, tiger moon, shark eye and canarium snails on the menu. The large melo melo, the tastiest, is grilled until soft and served with scallions and fried garlic; the price depends on its size. The rich variety of seafood options includes prawns, Halong squid, Venus clams and blood cockles. The steamed Venus clams with lemongrass, chilli and pineapple exude a deep umami flavour.

rows.name: Đông Phố
rows.address: 57 Ho Xuan Huong Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72407, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Popular among the locals and tourists alike, this unpretentious eatery shares a bungalow with an ice cream parlour and specialises in traditional Vietnamese dishes and French snacks. If you find the vast menu a bit daunting, the tasting menu is a great way to sample all the signature dishes. Try the assorted spring rolls, featuring a delightful variety of types on one plate, each filled with unique ingredients and crafted in different styles.

rows.name: Thúy 94 Cũ
rows.address: 84 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This popular restaurant specialises in crab, with a menu that shines the spotlight on the crustacean – crab spring rolls, fried rice, salt-baked crab, steamed crab… the list goes on. Crab vermicelli soup brims with umami-loaded crabmeat and roe. The broth features deep, slightly sweet flavours. Soft-shelled crab is fried to order, boasting a crispy crust and firm flesh. What’s more, crab can be replaced by shrimp in most dishes.

rows.name: Å by T.U.N.G
rows.address: 31-33 Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: With a ceiling mural of the Northern Lights, the airy dining space is a nod to chef Tung’s stint in Finland. On entering, diners first catch sight of the open kitchen before they are greeted by the chefs. Only one multi-course tasting menu is offered, and it changes every three months in line with the seasons. Chef Tung’s small plates are creative and original, paying tribute to Vietnamese food culture in terms of ingredients, flavours and techniques.

rows.name: Tales by Chapter
rows.address: 10 Nguyen Thanh Y Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Vietnam's first zero-waste, plant-based fine dining concept, this serene villa setting serves seasonal tasting menus based on local produce, rooftop-grown herbs and fermentation. Diners can see dishes being crafted at the chef's counter, such as corn pie tee – crisp cups of soy-corn purée, charred kernels, kimchi and fermented chilli – and chewy porcini-filled rice dumpling cake in a reimagined bánh bột lọc. Wine pairings, with or without alcohol, top off the experience.

rows.name: Chả Cá Anh Vũ (Ô Chợ Dừa)
rows.address: 120-K1 Giang Vo Street, O Cho Dua Ward, Hanoi, 11511, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Having been in the city for over 20 years, this bouncy family-run operation offers slick service. The homely vibe is depicted by chequered tablecloths, patterned wallpaper and brightly painted murals. Chả cá, grilled catfish seasoned with turmeric, is the name of the game here; its tender, juicy flesh carries a delicate aroma. You can also add nem cá, fish spring rolls; canh cá, fish soup; and lòng cá, fish stomach, as extras. The fresh, tasty food delivers an explosion of flavours and textures.

rows.name: Apero
rows.address: 45 Nguyen Duy Hieu Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Opened in 2022, this inviting ground-floor spot features large windows that let in ample natural light, fostering a relaxed mood. The open kitchen turns out unpretentious Italian fare, with lunch kept simple and more choice at dinnertime. Pasta is a highlight – try the rich and creamy carbonara with crispy bacon and parmesan. Save room for the house-made tiramisu, which is not overly sweet. Piano performances on Thu and Sun make this a great place to meet.

rows.name: Du Yên
rows.address: 26B Street 10, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Nestled in a quiet neighbourhood in town, this place occupies two levels with its room exuding rustic chic. The eclectic menu presents Vietnamese dishes plus Western and Thai options. Gỏi cuốn hoa bướm are the photogenic rice paper rolls adorned with edible pansies. The sweet peanut dip works well with the crisp vegetables. Męt bánh Huế is the vegetarian version of the famous steamed rice cake wrapped in banana leaves with fish sauce on the side.

rows.name: Luk Lak
rows.address: 28 Bach Dang Street, Hai Chau Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Perched on the banks of the Han River, this outpost of its Hanoian namesake boasts a dining room dripping in lush greenery. This branch shares the same culinary ethos as its flagship – creative Vietnamese fare packed with bold flavours. Grilled ground beef skewer with herbs and lemongrass seduces with aromas. Wrap in rice paper with veg and fruit for a hunger-quenching kick or pair with sticky rice and cassava root in a claypot.

rows.name: Elgin
rows.address: 27 Mac Dinh Chi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Orange banquettes and soft lighting enhance and offset the dark green wall tiles. Run by an energetic and passionate young team, Elgin can be relied upon to pamper its patrons. The menu, which changes regularly, showcases deftly prepared European dishes made mostly with local produce. Try the pork belly with fried brussels sprouts or gnocchi with lamb sugo, both of which are rich in flavours.

rows.name: Quince Eatery
rows.address: 37 Bis Ky Con Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This Colonial-style house with a vibrant decor, bistro-style furniture and soft lighting serves up a modern take on Mediterranean fare. Pick from a range of charcoal-grilled, wood-fired and oven-baked dishes and eat at the copper counter, which has six seats facing the open kitchen. Top choices include wild Hokkaido scallops and smoked marrow cappelletti, aged barbary duck breast and tasty golden berry with burnt sourdough mousse. Cocktails can be ordered from the bar upstairs.

rows.name: Cồ Đàm
rows.address: 68 Tran Hung Dao Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11019, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Named after the Buddha, Cồ Đàm’s eye-catching architecture boasts an ornate exterior inspired by Buddhist and Champa culture and a striking arched entrance of terracotta bricks. Four floors are open for dining, but the ground floor stands out for its tranquil pond and terracotta Buddha. The restaurant offers two set menus only — Vietnam Namaste and Cham Namaste — each showcasing creative, modern interpretations of beautifully presented Vietnamese classics, layered with rich flavour combinations.

rows.name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Hoành
rows.address: 66 To Hien Thanh Street, Bui Thi Xuan Ward, Hanoi, 112300, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This is among the busiest shops in the area because of its steamed rice rolls known as bánh cuốn. Rice noodle sheets are steamed to order and then wrapped around minced shiitake and pork. They also sell bún chả, or grilled pork noodles.

rows.name: Cơm Gà Lan
rows.address: 520 Trung Nu Vuong Street, Hoa Cuong Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: As the name suggests, there's only one thing on the menu – cơm gà, or chicken rice, but you can opt for the poultry roasted, steamed or shredded. Served with soup and pickles, the cơm gà xé bóp (shredded version), is especially popular. The lemongrass, coriander and onion lend the juicy chicken extra zing. Given the quality of the food and bargain prices, it's no surprise that this place is always jam-packed. Avoid peak hours.

rows.name: Si Dining
rows.address: 1 Giang Chau 2 Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: This al fresco Italian dining spot is known for its daily catch. The chef's passion for fish shines through in his fresh, seasonal dishes, served in signature set menus or à la carte. With soft lighting for a romantic atmosphere, the establishment occupies two floors, with a bar downstairs and the dining room upstairs. The paintings on the walls, by local artists, are available for purchase. The wine pairings complete the experience.

rows.name: Cô Liêng
rows.address: 321 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72407, Vietnam
rows.description_en: For nearly 30 years, this humble spot has been serving authentic Southern Vietnamese flavours. The highlight is the charcoal-grilled bò lá lốt, minced beef wrapped in betel leaves, with its well-balanced savoury-sweet taste. A charcoal grill at the entrance sends smoky aromas into the street as each order is freshly prepared. The grilled meats can be enjoyed with fresh herbs and vegetables or with bánh hỏi, rice vermicelli bundles.

rows.name: The Monkey Gallery Dining
rows.address: 3F, 91 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Three wise founders, all born in the Year of the Monkey, have created a relaxed “gallery” with minimalist, Japanese-influenced décor, where the food takes centre stage. A concrete counter faces the open kitchen, led by a young chef from Central Vietnam, who draws on local dishes and produce from his roots, refined through European culinary training. The restaurant focuses on a full tasting menu, with optional add-ons, alongside wine, non-alcoholic pairings, and a creative list of cocktails and mocktails.

rows.name: Ngon Garden
rows.address: 70 Nguyen Du Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 112310, Vietnam
rows.description_en: On the banks of Thien Quang Lake, this restaurant, reminiscent of an Indochinese-style villa, boasts a patio surrounded by lush greenery. The menu features specialities from all over Vietnam, alongside Asian delicacies of Chinese and Thai origins. From the century-old Bat Dan phở recipe from Hanoi and bún bò huế grilled beef from Nha Trang to fresh veggies from Dalat and live seafood from all over the world, every dish is deftly crafted and delicately seasoned. A favourite in Hanoi, especially for its garden seating, the restaurant is very popular, so advance booking is highly recommended.

rows.name: Bún Chả Hương Liên
rows.address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Hai Ba Trung Ward, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
rows.description_en: Playing on their claim to fame, this joint displays photos of its celebrity guests alongside the glass-encased “president table.” Ordering is straightforward, with most guests opting for the “Obama Combo”, which includes a fried seafood roll, a bowl of the special bún chả and a bia hà nội. The bún chả itself delivers a satisfying blend of rustic flavours, with smoky pork, meat patties, fragrant herbs and fresh salad leaves. Payment is made in cash at the entrance on departure.
